title: An irreducible group scheme over a field is quasi-compact
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $H$ be a group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. If the underlying space $|H|$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components], then $H$ is quasi-compact: every open covering of $|H|$ has a finite subcover [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No finite-type, smoothness or reducedness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose $K/k$ for $X=H$ by [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson], and put $G=H_K$. Base change the multiplication, unit and inverse; the group diagrams remain equalities by the fibre-product universal property [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]. We check irreducibility, without assuming geometric irreducibility of an arbitrary irreducible scheme. By [lem-sfb-group-local-minimal-prime], the reduced identity component $Z$ is geometrically irreducible. Here $H$ is irreducible, so its only irreducible component is the whole space and $Z=H_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $Z_K\to H_K$ is a homeomorphism; $Z_K$ is irreducible by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], so $G$ is irreducible. Thus $G$ is an irreducible group scheme over $K$, is Jacobson, and all its closed points have residue field $K$.

source.place: Tag 0B7P, first paragraph; Tag 047M, lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible; Tag 0479 in varieties.tex.

proof.text: The multiplication $m:G\times_KG\to G$ is open. Indeed the group diagrams [def-sc-group-scheme] make $s(x,y)=(xy,y)$ an isomorphism with inverse $s^{-1}(z,y)=(zy^{-1},y)$, since $(xy)y^{-1}=x$ and $(zy^{-1})y=z$ on every test scheme. Moreover $m=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ s$. The first projection is open by [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open], applied with the factors interchanged. An isomorphism induces a homeomorphism, so the displayed factorization proves openness of $m$.

source.place: Tag 047K, lemma-group-scheme-over-field-open-multiplication, the shear isomorphism; Morphisms Tag 0383, lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open.

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq G$: the unit supplies a point and the defining affine neighbourhoods of a scheme supply such a $U$ [def-pc-scheme]. The inverse $i$ is an isomorphism, since $i^2=\mathrm{id}$ by [def-sc-group-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $U\times_KU$ is an open subscheme of $G\times_KG$. The automorphism $\mathrm{id}\times i$ therefore carries it to an open subset. Step 2 now says that the image $W$ of $d:U\times_KU\to G$, $(u,v)\mapsto uv^{-1}$, is open.

source.place: Tag 0B7P, second paragraph; Tag 047K for the openness calculation.

proof.text: Fix $g\in G(K)$. Left translation $t_g(x)=gx$ has inverse $t_{g^{-1}}$ by the group diagrams [def-sc-group-scheme]. Thus $gU$ and $U$ are nonempty open subsets. Their intersection is nonempty by [def-weil-irreducible-components]: otherwise their closed complements would express the irreducible space as a union of two proper closed subsets. Since the closed points are dense and rational by step 1, choose a closed point $a$ in this intersection. Its residue-field isomorphism makes it a $K$-point; it factors through both open subschemes. Set $b=t_{g^{-1}}(a)\in U(K)$. Then $a=gb$ and $d(a,b)=ab^{-1}=g$. Hence $W$ contains every $K$-point and therefore every closed point of $G$. If $G\setminus W$ were nonempty, the Jacobson property of [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson] applied to this closed subset would put a closed point in it. Thus $d$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0B7P, second paragraph: intersect gU with U, then use rational closed points and the Jacobson property.

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U\times_KU\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_KA)$ is affine. The projection $G=H_K\to H$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]: $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective, since both spectra have one point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Composing this projection with the surjective map $d$ of step 4 gives a surjective morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_KA)\to H$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasicompact-affine-surjection] to obtain quasi-compactness of $H$, exactly the asserted finite-subcover property.

source.place: Tag 0B7P, first and last sentences of the proof; affine fibre product and surjective affine-source criterion.
